producer_report.summary: Raised the agent ceiling to 16 (athena.toml max_concurrency 12), made the `athena drain --help` ceiling come from the constant, and added a per-run record of group sizes. Root cause of the earlier major finding: the help was a literal string separate from MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING. It now holds a `{MAX_CONCURRENCY}` placeholder that `cli_command()` in main.rs fills from the constant. A test checks the rendered help against the constant. `Report.group_sizes` lists the item count of each plan group worked, in order. A group counts only if one of its items got a job line, so a stop before the group starts leaves it out. display::drain prints `groups      N worked, sizes ..., mean X.X` only when something was worked. Docs (async-drain.md, parallel-jobs.md, step 6 Built note) and CHANGELOG (Added and Fixed) are updated.

open_issues: Under a serial drain (one_at_a_time) a group is split and its remainder is taken up again as a smaller group on the next wave, so group_sizes then reads as sizes of the remaining batches, not original group sizes. It is recorded as the batch stood when taken up.
I did not read the full `cargo test -p athena-cli` output, only that the command succeeded. The `cargo fmt --check` run is left to Athena.
mistakes: My first version recorded the group size before running it, so a group that the job limit stopped before any job started was still recorded. The unreached-group test caught it, and I fixed it by recording only after an item of the group has a job line.
learnings: clap derive after_help attributes must be literals, so a placeholder filled in `Cli::command().mut_subcommand` is the way to derive text from a constant.

The drain job limit is noticed only when the next group tries to start its first job, so a group can be taken from the plan without any job running. group_sizes counts a group only once one of its items has a job line.
Report is built in exactly one place (drain_with), so adding a field touched only that constructor plus the new display test.
